title: Civil Protection Centre / Roland Baldi Architects
text:
Civil Protection Centre / Roland Baldi Architects

Set between the wooded slopes of the Venosta Valley and Oris – a hamlet in Lasa - the new Civil Protection Centre makes a confident architectural statement. Constructed from green-pigmented insulating concrete, the building seamlessly blends the functional requirements of the volunteer fire department with a distinctive architectural expression. Its monolithic appearance lends the structure a powerful identity, while its color establishes a subtle dialogue with the surrounding landscape.

title: The Cultural Life of Colors in Latin American Interiors
text:
The Cultural Life of Colors in Latin American Interiors

A color has a biography. A color can have an origin, but it can also transform. It can move between materials and disciplines, from a local practice into architecture, from something ordinary into something symbolic. It can lose one association and acquire another, or persist without anyone consciously thinking of it as cultural. Its life unfolds through the conditions in which it is produced, used, repeated, and inhabited. As these conditions change, so do the meanings a color can carry.

title: Toyota City Museum / Shigeru Ban Architects
text:
Toyota City Museum / Shigeru Ban Architects

Toyota City Museum is planned to be located on the east side of the site, just like the adjacent Toyota Municipal Museum of Art, to allow for integrated site utilization. The western side of the site is designed as a continuous landscape with the art museum, serving the role of integrating the two sites.

title: "A Place Remembers What Has Happened:" Tsuyoshi Tane on Memory as a Design Driver in Louisiana Channel Interview
text:
"A Place Remembers What Has Happened:" Tsuyoshi Tane on Memory as a Design Driver in Louisiana Channel Interview

Tsuyoshi Tane is a Japanese architect born in 1979 in Tokyo and based in Paris, where he founded ATTA – Atelier Tsuyoshi Tane Architects in 2006. Working across cultural, institutional, and landscape-related projects, Tane has developed an architectural approach that positions memory as a fundamental design driver. In his interview with Louisiana Channel, filmed in his Paris studio, Tane reflects on architecture as a discipline of observation and thought, arguing that meaningful design emerges from carefully reading the traces embedded within a site. For him, architecture is not produced on a blank slate but begins with an inquiry into what already exists, physically, culturally, and emotionally, beneath the surface of a place.

title: Ceramics Workshop in Copenhagen / Jesper Kusk Arkitekter
text:
Ceramics Workshop in Copenhagen / Jesper Kusk Arkitekter

The small ceramics workshop is located on the corner of a site in Valby, Copenhagen. Upon arrival, the workshop's south façade comes into view, nestled among the greenery beneath an apple tree. During the day, the surrounding greenery is reflected in the façade's windows, while in the evening, the workshop illuminates its surroundings.

title: “Cities Are Mental Weapons”: Utopian Hours 2026 Returns to Turin with Sir Peter Cook and a Program on City-Making
text:
“Cities Are Mental Weapons”: Utopian Hours 2026 Returns to Turin with Sir Peter Cook and a Program on City-Making

The second part of the Utopian Hours 2026 international city-making festival will be held in Turin on October 16 and 17. After a first chapter in Rotterdam, the festival is marking its tenth anniversary edition by returning to its hometown in Italy. The event's lineup and cultural program are designed to explore how cities can respond creatively to the social, environmental, and political challenges of the 21st century. The Utopian Hours festival has been organized since 2017 by Stratosferica, a nonprofit cultural association dedicated to producing and sharing urban knowledge through content on the evolution of cities, urban communication strategies, events, community building and placemaking.

title: When the Outdoors Becomes Home: A New Generation of Outdoor Kitchens
text:
When the Outdoors Becomes Home: A New Generation of Outdoor Kitchens

Outdoor kitchens have evolved from exclusive luxury additions into natural extensions of the home. Gardens, terraces, and porches are being transformed into spaces for cooking and, above all, entertaining without having to step inside. This solution not only adds convenience but also increases property value, responding to a lifestyle that is increasingly connected to the outdoors.

title: Bunkers and Arks: Escaping the Future We Built Ourselves
text:
Bunkers and Arks: Escaping the Future We Built Ourselves

Inverting the conventional narrative, this story begins at the end. The day after the world's collapse. While almost the entire population struggles to survive flames and solar storms, a tiny fraction is greeted by a heavily armed guard at the entrance to the Survival Condo Project, a former missile silo in Kansas converted a few years ago into luxury apartments.

title: Port Melbourne Secondary College / Billard Leece Partnership
text:
Port Melbourne Secondary College / Billard Leece Partnership

Port Melbourne Secondary College (PMSC) is the first vertical school as part of Australia's biggest urban rejuvenation project, Fishermans Bend. Designed by Billard Leece Partnership (BLP), the school is within a designated precinct for advanced technology, innovation and education where, over the next 30 years, 80,000 people will live, work and study. The development gives Port Melbourne a new, forward-thinking learning hub for students and the local community who have access to the library, gym, food technology and art spaces after hours.

title: Minoudar House / harandi & harandi architects
text:
Minoudar House / harandi & harandi architects

In the historic core of Yazd, a UNESCO World Heritage city on the edge of Iran's central desert, Harandi & Harandi Architects have carefully revived a 400-year-old dwelling and transformed it into Minoudar House, a three-room boutique hotel where heritage conservation itself becomes the driving design idea.

title: Integrating Solar Protection as an Envelope Strategy
text:
Integrating Solar Protection as an Envelope Strategy

Heat waves are becoming more and more frequent worldwide, prompting architects to reconsider how building envelopes are conceived and designed. The focus is no longer solely on limiting heat loss during the colder months, but also on controlling how much heat enters buildings during periods of intense solar radiation. By understanding solar shading as a design decision rather than a decorative or interior-conditioning element, it becomes part of passive energy-efficiency strategies that can contribute to thermal and visual comfort while reducing cooling demand.

title: Yanqing Li Commercial Renovation / Mix Architecture
text:
Yanqing Li Commercial Renovation / Mix Architecture

Yanqing Li is located in Hankou's historic district, at the intersection of Shengli Street and Eryao Xiaolu. It consists of seven buildings blending Eastern and Western styles, arranged around four intertwined alleyways. Originally built in 1933 by Zhong Yansheng, this traditional lifen was named after him. Having suffered wartime damage and later population shifts, it is now being revitalized through urban regeneration. The client envisions transforming it into an open commercial block while preserving its historic character, making it a pilot project for the Sanyang district renewal.

title: ITA - Italian Trade Agency Dakar / MOST Monti Studio
text:
ITA - Italian Trade Agency Dakar / MOST Monti Studio

Within the complex of the Italian Embassy in Dakar, Senegal, the new headquarters of ITA, the Italian Trade Agency, responsible for promoting Italian businesses abroad and supporting their internationalization, was created through the rehabilitation of an abandoned building. More than a simple functional conversion, the project embraces reuse as an architectural and cultural choice, proposing an alternative to the construction of an entirely new office building in the city centre.

title: Wise Consultation Office / RVMN
text:
Wise Consultation Office / RVMN

It is said that trees sway in order not to be shaken. Because they move with flexibility, they are able to remain rooted in their place and continue to grow over time. Marriage, too, is a journey that can be calm at times and shift in unexpected directions, and therefore requires a flexible attitude. In the first WISE space, this perspective on marriage and the idea of flexibility were translated into a design language. Flexible curves and spatial flows were used to create both direct and indirect separation between the circulation and sightlines of waiting customers and those receiving consultations, preventing them from directly interfering with one another.

title: Pinewood Houses / NOMO STUDIO
text:
Pinewood Houses / NOMO STUDIO

Set in a small village on Spain's northern Mediterranean coast, Pinewood Houses comprises two single-family homes embedded within a pine forest near the beach on the Costa Brava. The project is guided by a clear premise: to place the two dwellings in an intercalated arrangement that avoids mutual obstruction, allowing each house to breathe and maintaining long visual depth across the site.

title: Ība House / Daniel Fromer
text:
Ība House / Daniel Fromer

The landscape designer Rodrigo Oliveira was enchanted by a plot of just over five thousand square meters in southern Bahia. With a topography reminiscent of a natural amphitheater, facing the landscape and offering a privileged view of the sunset, Casa ĪBA nestles among natural and designed gardens, always respecting the original topography of the site.

title: L'AIGUILLEUSE - Renovation of a former railway signal box into a kiosk-bar / Studio Téré
text:
L'AIGUILLEUSE - Renovation of a former railway signal box into a kiosk-bar / Studio Téré

"L'Aiguilleuse" is a project that transforms a former 1960s railway signal box into a small kiosk-bar located at the heart of the Jardins de l'Estuaire, a new public park on the Île de Nantes, France. Originally part of the Nantes-État railway infrastructure, the building once controlled train movements entering the station. As the surrounding railway landscape gradually disappeared, the signal box remained as a small but distinctive fragment of the site's industrial history.

title: Chaume Sublimé / COAT
text:
Chaume Sublimé / COAT

Chaume Sublimé is an ephemeral installation for Montpellier's Festival des Architectures Vives 2025 that elevates humble reed grass into a sensory and atmospheric experience, celebrating both sustainability and craftsmanship.

title: Designing the In-Between: From Tactical Interventions to Urban Policy in Barcelona
text:
Designing the In-Between: From Tactical Interventions to Urban Policy in Barcelona

In Europe, cities are confronting the challenge of adapting existing urban conditions to a changing climate and warming summers while improving access to nature, quality public spaces, and the resources of everyday routines. ReGreeneration, a Horizon Europe initiative working across nine European cities, approaches this challenge through urban renaturing at the neighborhood scale. Combining strategies for complete neighborhoods, communal spaces, and nature-based solutions for cities, the Barcelona project examines how climate adaptation is embedded within residual, peripheral spaces of daily life. As part of a series following ReGreeneration across the participating cities, this article turns to Barcelona, where the project is working in the Trinitat Nova neighborhood to explore how small, often overlooked, urban spaces contribute to broader models of regeneration.

title: Home Herengracht / Studio Modijefsky
text:
Home Herengracht / Studio Modijefsky

Nestled in central Amsterdam on the prestigious Herengracht, this canal-side apartment enjoys expansive views over the water while remaining sheltered by the lush trees surrounding the façade. Studio Modijefsky was commissioned to redesign the entrance sequence, guest facilities, kitchen, and pantry, while refining the circulation towards the private quarters of the home. The result is an interior that balances bold material gestures with a calm and timeless spatial experience.

title: RESONANCE - Tallinn Architecture Biennale Installation / Aru Ma- Architects
text:
RESONANCE - Tallinn Architecture Biennale Installation / Aru Ma- Architects

Set against Tallinn's rapidly commercializing urban backdrop, the installation offers a sheltered courtyard detached from its surroundings, creating a deliberate pause. Here, the sea breeze whispers against silent stones, and sunlight filters onto the warm, sweeping curves of plywood screens. It is a spatial privilege carved from ordinary materials, filtering out external chaos for pure atmospheric luxury.

title: Mahachai Residence / Patara Architects
text:
Mahachai Residence / Patara Architects

Mahachai Residence occupies a riverside plot on the Tha Chin River, on land once occupied by the owner's boat-repair warehouse. Rather than erase this history, the house is conceived as a day-use villa, a place for the owner to rest, take in the river, and watch it turn gold at sunset, quietly carrying the memory of the site's working past into its structure and materials.

title: Prukpirom House Renovation (PPR House) / S+S Architects
text:
Prukpirom House Renovation (PPR House) / S+S Architects

Prukpirom House Renovation transforms a family home that has stood for more than 29 years. Located on a generous site surrounded by mature greenery, the existing house offered opportunities to expand and reorganize the living spaces while retaining its relationship with the garden.

title: La Negrita House / Estudio Palacios
text:
La Negrita House / Estudio Palacios

Situated on the shores of Los Molinos Lake and surrounded by a dense eucalyptus forest, La Negrita embodies the desire for a peaceful retreat amid a beautiful, playful atmosphere with its own unique microclimate.
